intention: The bus delivers: an envelope posted to a device is handed to that device's shim and a receipt is written, so that posting mail and mail arriving stop being the same observation.
why: Measured 2026-08-11: BaseShim.deliver — the method that hands an envelope to a device and wakes it — had stood with ZERO CALLERS since the day it was written. post wrote durable envelopes, read returned them whole, and nothing on earth drained an inbox. From the sender's side that is indistinguishable from a working bus: the post succeeds, the row lands, the read shows it sitting there. Three envelopes were in transit when this was found, the oldest addressed to a device that has never once looked. This ticket is the second half of the ground-loop discovery work: the loop discovered its devices and pulsed them, and the mail still went nowhere.
traces_to: Law 7 (a message that cannot be delivered must not fail silently — the trouble lane's founding example in Akien's own 2026-07-25 words); Law 6 (the owner of the traffic delivers it: the postman is the BUS's own shim, never the heartbeat, because handing an envelope to its addressee is ROUTING and the ground_loop does not route); Law 1 (the roster the heartbeat already publishes is reused rather than a second registry minted, so nothing new can go stale).

receipts.proofs_run_green_twice: ground_loop 21, discovery 12, bus 6, delivery 10, shim 7 = 56 teeth; the five librarian proofs green beside them
receipts.live_fire: 2026-08-11 against the real bus: the first drain reported 2x no_shim ('dave') and 1x no_receiver (harbor_master), and the resident loop was restarted to pick up the postman (pid 3887729, 'bus' first on the roster). Every finding it reported was true.
receipts.what_the_proof_killed: The bench gate this same session shipped with. _refresh_bench stat'd the trouble DIRECTORY's mtime, but trouble._write rewrites the ticket file IN PLACE — no temp, no rename — so a clear never moves that mtime and a benched device would have stayed benched forever while every surface reported a healthy beat. Replaced by an entry fingerprint (name, mtime, size per .json), and pinned by a tooth that asserts the directory mtime is UNCHANGED across the clear so the tooth cannot pass by accident.
design_decisions_worth_keeping: The deliverer is the bus's own shim, not the heartbeat: ground_loop 'does NOT execute, resolve, schedule, ROUTE, or write' — that clause is the 584aa74 goof's headstone, and handing an envelope to its addressee is routing.

Delivery is an append-only receipt in a sibling table, never a column on the envelope: a RECORD channel may not be rewritten (Law 7), and create_owned_table is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS so a new column would need a migration.

The receipt is written AFTER the device takes the envelope, so a raising receiver leaves the mail in the inbox. At-least-once is the right side to fail on — losing a record of truth is worse than delivering twice.
Findings are deduped per envelope (_reported), because undeliverable mail stays undeliverable: without it, one stuck envelope reports the identical finding once a second forever.

The bus emits, not the shim: emit is DiagnosticBase's (devices), and a shim RECEIVES breadcrumbs rather than sending them — which is also the right ownership, since the stuck message is the bus's fact.
receipts.filed_edge: The drain is asked on a cadence because the beat is what exists today. The event-shaped answer is the store telling the postman a row landed (Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY through db_domain's gate), turning one query per second into zero queries until there is mail. It waits on real volume and on db_domain growing a listen face — its owner's call, not the bus's.
